headline: The Co-op's legal services arm is using AI to record and score every probate phone call its advisers take, which a whistleblower calls "oppressive and dystopian".
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a clear example of AI monitoring of workers, with company and union views, but on a small group of staff.
importance_line: Dozens of advisers who deal with bereaved customers are now scored by AI on each call, and the Co-op says it is only a support tool, so the harm described rests on one anonymous worker and union comment.
summary: The Guardian reports that Co-op Legal Services uses an OpenAI model to record and score calls between advisers and customers seeking help with probate, wills and estates, rating more than 50 aspects of each call and sending pass or fail results to managers. A whistleblower calls it "oppressive and dystopian", while the Co-op says the AI is a support tool, not a decision-maker, and a union and the International Labour Organization warn about stress and weak rules on workplace AI monitoring.
